annotation.title_clean: The theological ethics of human enhancement: Genetic engineering, robotics and nanotechnology
annotation.title_en: The theological ethics of human enhancement: Genetic engineering, robotics and nanotechnology
annotation.venue: In die Skriflig / In Luce Verbi
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed South African theology article examining bioethical challenges of human enhancement via genetic engineering, robotics and nanotechnology, drawing on Christian anthropology and imago Dei and public theology. It doesn't argue a specific position but identifies issues and future research areas, including human dignity and capabilities.
key_provisions_or_claims: Human enhancement technologies outpace ethical reflection, raising 'playing God' debates.
Enhancement defined as improvement beyond normal, distinct from therapy.
Christian anthropology (imago Dei) offers a basis for public and prophetic response.
Human dignity and capabilities approaches inform evaluation of enhancements.
Identifies gaps for future research rather than advancing a specific position.
